thread:
maya: Heads-up — saw a p99 spike after the microbatch config change this morning. p95 improved (~10%) but p99 went up ~2x during cross-region fallback windows. Digging in now.

ravi: Which microbatch change? we moved default from 4 -> 12 in the auto-batching heuristic yesterday right?

maya: yep, that change. Baseline traffic shows better throughput but when requests route to fallback region we get cold KV-cache + different kernel selection and a tail amplification.

olga: can you paste the profiler output?

maya: posting condensed profiler snippet from the 10:05 incident window:
```
2026-03-18T10:05:12Z PROFILE_SUMMARY: p99 latency 1320ms (baseline 640ms)
kernel_choice: aten_flash_attn_v2 (80% success) -> fallback to aten_generic (20%)
kv_cache_stats: cache_miss_rate spike from 3% -> 37% across routed shard B
microbatch_sizes: avg_batch=10, variance high (2..12)
osched_backpressure: observed 14% backpressure events
```

sam: that kernel mismatch looks bad — if KV misses cause longer seq lengths or more key lookups we can be forced onto the generic kernel with horrible perf.

ken: also likely that cache eviction rate correlated with cross-region latency: fallback routing increases end-to-end time and those in-flight requests grow queue depth, amplifying async evictions.

maya: agreed. timeline suggests: 1) upstream route failover -> more requests to eu-west fallback cluster 2) cache warming not complete for certain model shards -> KV misses spike 3) kernel selector picks slower path for those sequences -> microbatching tries to pack but variance causes head-of-line blocking -> p99 blowup.

ravi: Do we have a simple repro? maybe run replay against eu-west with forced kernel patch?

maya: repro steps I used locally:
```bash
# replay sample traffic with legacy routing delay
rt-replay --trace_kernel --target-region eu-west --concurrency 120 --seed 8421 traces/2026-03-18/10-05-fallback.json
# enable verbose kv logging and kernel selector
export RT_LOG=kv:debug,kernel:debug
```
Gave identical kernel fallback pattern.

olga: quick mitigation options: 1) reduce microbatch max size to 6 for fallback routes, 2) bias kernel selector towards the optimized kernel unless explicit incompatibility, 3) aggressive prefix caching for routed shards. Which do you want to try first?

sam: I vote for 1 + 3 at the same time. Reduce microbatch on fallback and pre-warm KV prefixes for shards that are candidate fallbacks. Should buy us p99 headroom.

ken: we should also add a circuit-breaker: when cross-region requests exceed X/s route a percentage to local degraded model (quantized) to keep latency SLOs.

maya: good call. I'll send a small canary for microbatch max 6 for fallback-only policy. Can someone flip the routing flag?

deploy-bot: canary deploy started by maya on eng-runtime/fallback-microbatch-config (id: canary-1917801234)

ravi: I pushed a lightweight KV pre-warm hook to the fallback-init path — it seeds top prefixes for active customers. Note: pre-warm increases short-term memory footprint but should reduce misses.

maya: After canary metrics (10m) — p99 improved from 1320ms -> 720ms during a synthetic failover window. p95 unchanged (still slightly better than old). Looks promising.

olga: any evidence that kernel selector bias is safe? we don't want silent correctness regressions.

sam: tested on canary traffic: biased selector preferred aten_flash_attn_v2 for sequences under 2048 tokens only when quantization/profile flags matched. Added runtime assertion to fall back immediately if output lengths != expected. No diffs on unit evals.

maya: next steps:
- roll fallback microbatch max 6 to 25% traffic (maya)
- monitor p95/p99 and kv_miss_rate (sre)
- add dashboard widget for kernel_choice breakout by region (ravi)
- implement circuit-breaker policy for extreme cross-zone surge (ken)

ken: logging ticket filed: RT-4672 (circuit-breaker policy spec)

sre-bot: alert-silenced for canary window. Metrics: canary p99 720ms, control p99 1280ms, kv_miss_rate down from 37% -> 8%.

maya: thanks team. we'll leave canary running for 2h and reconvene if any regressions show. ping me if you see a different kernel failure mode. :thumbsup:
